senses.sense_definition: A pattern formed by concentric circles, curves, or a spiral.

examples.text: The artist decorated the vase with an intricate <w>whorl</w> that drew the viewer's eye inwards.
Carved into the ancient stone was a distinct <w>whorl</w> representing the sun.

senses.sense_definition: A spiral or circular pattern found on the human body, such as in a fingerprint or the ridges of an ear.

examples.text: Forensic experts examined the unique <w>whorl</w> left behind in the print at the scene.
Each person has a distinctive <w>whorl</w> on the tips of their fingers.

senses.sense_definition: An arrangement of three or more leaves, flowers, or other plant organs radiating from the same node on a stem.

examples.text: The botanist identified the plant species by the symmetrical <w>whorl</w> of leaves growing at each node.
Bright purple petals formed a neat <w>whorl</w> at the top of the slender stem.

senses.sense_definition: A single complete turn or spiral in the shell of a snail or univalve mollusk.

examples.text: The outer <w>whorl</w> of the snail shell showed noticeable ridges and varied coloration.
As the mollusk grows, it gradually adds a new <w>whorl</w> to expand its protective shell.

senses.sense_definition: A weighted ring or disc fitted onto a spindle to maintain rotational momentum while spinning thread.

examples.text: Archaeologists uncovered a small clay <w>whorl</w> that was once used to spin wool into yarn.
The heavy stone <w>whorl</w> helped the wooden spindle keep turning steadily.

senses.sense_definition: To move in, or form, a circular or spiraling pattern.

examples.text: Autumn leaves began to <w>whorl</w> across the garden as the sudden gust picked up.
The mist continued to <w>whorl</w> above the cool surface of the quiet mountain lake.
